$comment: Template-side facts, kept separate from fleet.json so the build description
of an app and its packaging on Unraid can change independently.
visibility — checked with `gh repo view` on 2026-08-05, not assumed. The
eight browser tools were published on 2026-08-05, so nothing in the fleet
is private any more; the machinery below is kept because it is the reason
the generated output looks the way it does, and because a future app may
well start private again.
It decides three things that all fail quietly if got wrong:
1. GHCR packages inherit their repo's visibility on first publish. A
template in a public Community Applications store pointing at a private
package gives every user who clicks Install a manifest-unknown or
denied error, which reads like a broken template rather than a
permissions one. Private apps therefore go to templates-private/ and
are installed on your own server via Add Container, not via CA.
2. GitHub Actions minutes are only consumed by private repositories.
Public repos build for free, so they carry a pull_request trigger; a
private one would be push-only on main, building an image once per
landed change rather than on every PR push. No repo bills today.
3. raw.githubusercontent.com 404s for private repos, so an icon URL
pointing there renders as a broken image in CA. Private templates get
no icon rather than a dead link.
hostPort — the default host port the template offers. Assigned so that a
server running several of these at once has no collisions out of the box.
Static sites take 8500+; services keep the port they natively listen on,
because their config files, companion modules and documentation all name
it and a template that quietly remapped it would contradict them.
Apps on host networking have no hostPort: the container binds the host's
port directly and the template cannot remap it.

profile.text: Stoatworks Labs builds open tooling for live AV: video routing and switcher control, audio measurement and loudness, lighting and LED design, RF coordination, and Resolume/OpenFX plugins. This repository holds the Unraid templates for the ones that make sense on a server — the always-on services (ATEM fleet monitoring, SRT routing, device discovery, CasparCG show control, RF coordination) alongside the browser-based calculators and design tools, which run entirely in the browser and are worth self-hosting so they work in a venue with no internet. Images are built by GitHub Actions and published to GHCR. Anything that discovers devices over mDNS or broadcast ships with host networking, because Docker's bridge network silently finds nothing. Support is via GitHub issues on each project.
